implementationPlan.description:
docs/MCP_SERVER.md: the two tool sections (DoD 1). Use the Edit tool in your task worktree W (a TOOL witness). Write everything from the landed source, field for field; never from the task text.

Placement: insert `### moe.get_execution_readiness`, then `### moe.get_seat_liveness`, directly after the `### moe.heartbeat` section, before `### moe.lease_account`. Each heading must be exactly `### moe.<name>` with nothing after it, because util/taskTimeBudgetDocs.test.ts TOOL_HEADING reads tool sections that way. Follow the house style of the neighbouring wrapper-only sections: a lead sentence, **Parameters:** and **Returns:** in typescript blocks, then bullets.

moe.get_execution_readiness (source: packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getExecutionReadiness.ts; holder delivery/readinessHolder.ts; gate delivery/executionProfile.ts assertExecutionProfileReady):
- Wrapper-only: TOOL_AUDIENCE 'wrapper' in tools/index.ts, so no role sees it in tools/list.
- It is read-only. It writes no state, appends no activity and touches no worker, and it grants nothing: claims and progression are still gated by the same held evaluation in assertExecutionProfileReady (EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY).
- Parameters: `refresh?: boolean`; `workerId` is injected by the proxy and never read.
- Returns exactly `{ profile, ready, missingCapabilities, evaluatedAt }`:
  - `profile`: the live resolveExecutionProfile, or 'unreadable' for a malformed executionProfile setting;
  - `missingCapabilities`: a filter over READINESS_IDS, in that order. Point at the TROUBLESHOOTING.md table from step 3;
  - `evaluatedAt`: null when the evaluator has never run or the last evaluation failed.
- `refresh: true`:
  - re-runs the daemon's own evaluator (refreshReadiness with production inputs), and the call awaits it;
  - is single-flight: a concurrent call joins the run in flight;
  - starts a new run only when READINESS_REFRESH_WINDOW_MS (30 s) has passed since the last start, or the clock went backwards.
- Its error handling:
  - a non-boolean refresh is INVALID_INPUT naming `refresh`;
  - a failed evaluation never fails the read, because the holder fails closed.
- `blocking: true`: it runs outside the fleet-wide state mutex because a refresh awaits a bounded evaluation (probe 10 s, guard 11 s). It never parks.
- The /ws twin, in the same section: `{ type: 'GET_EXECUTION_READINESS', payload?: { refresh?: boolean } }` answers `{ type: 'EXECUTION_READINESS', payload }` with the same four fields. It is read-only like GET_METRICS and needs no mutex. A non-boolean refresh answers ERROR 'GET_EXECUTION_READINESS refresh must be a boolean', and any failure answers ERROR 'GET_EXECUTION_READINESS failed', with no detail, path or stack. Source: server/WebSocketServer.ts, case 'GET_EXECUTION_READINESS'.
- Add one line under `## Plugin WebSocket Messages`, after the capability-negotiation subsection, naming the message pair and linking to this section.

moe.get_seat_liveness (source: tools/getSeatLiveness.ts and state/attemptStore.ts countOpenAttempts; consumer: scripts/local-runner/vm-control.mjs seatStateOf):
- Wrapper-only and read-only. It runs under the state mutex (no blocking flag) and writes nothing.
- Parameters: `workerId: string`, required. This is the seat inspected, not the caller. It must be non-blank, at most 255 characters and free of control characters, else INVALID_INPUT naming `workerId`. When the caller omits it, moe-proxy injects the caller's own MOE_WORKER_ID, so the call then reports on the caller itself.
- Returns exactly `{ workerId, registered, status, openAttempts }`:
  - `registered`: a worker record exists;
  - `status`: that record's status, else null;
  - `openAttempts`: the attempts carrying this workerId in phase running, finalizing or reconciling.
- A seat is gone only when `(!registered || status === 'DEAD') && openAttempts === 0`. vm-control.mjs maps a registered, non-DEAD seat to 'registered', else openAttempts > 0 to 'attempt-open', else 'gone'. A malformed reply is 'unknown' and keeps the VM.
- A match never proves a process is alive or dead: the runner's own liveness is vm-control.mjs runnerProbe.

The task's other deliverable: executionRoute 'vm' is already documented on claim_next_task (**Execution route**, about :1479 at 0fa7750e) and wait_for_task (about :1632 and :1641). Verify it against tools/claimNextTask.ts and waitForTask.ts, change nothing there, and say so in the summary.

(a) serverCapabilities, under `## Plugin WebSocket Messages` > Optional client capability negotiation (about :3360):
- In the `capabilities` map, `verifiedLocal: false` becomes `verifiedLocal: true` (server/clientCapabilities.ts SERVER_CAPABILITIES; true since CQ-M07d2).
- The example's `negotiatedCapabilities.verifiedLocal` stays false, which is correct for that hello: it sent only planRevisions, and negotiated means server support AND client literal true. Say so in one short clause, so the remaining `false` reads as intended.
- In the paragraph that starts 'Capabilities describe **wire support, not authentication, trusted evidence or readiness**', replace 'verified-local stays unconditionally unavailable even for a fully capable client with a matching revision'. The replacement says: verifiedLocal is wire support for the readiness projection (moe.get_execution_readiness and GET_EXECUTION_READINESS), never readiness, and verified-local is admitted only while the daemon's held evaluation is ready (assertExecutionProfileReady); a client claim never grants it.

(b) The same stale claim at about :464 ('Passing grants entry only, never readiness: `verified-local` stays unavailable (`EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY`) at claim and at progression'): reword it to say that a strict claim or progression still needs the held readiness, else EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY.

(c) The six strict-consumer sentences, task-7aa6be67's residuals. They were cited at 154a1c71's lines 1242, 1249, 1274, 1464, 1508 and 1996; at 0fa7750e they are:
- :1255 report_blocked Un-block routes, '(auto, all `blockedOnTaskIds` DONE/ARCHIVED)';
- :1262 the response comment '// Every named prerequisite already DONE/ARCHIVED (fresh flip, no resourceId)';
- :1287 'satisfiedBlockedOnTaskIds?: … (DONE/ARCHIVED, judged as the auto-unblock judges them)';
- :1485 claim_next_task BLOCKED hold, 'a set `blockedOnTaskIds` means it auto-unblocks when every listed task is DONE/ARCHIVED';
- :1529 'blockedOnTaskIds?: string[] // BLOCKED holds only; set = auto-unblocks when all are DONE/ARCHIVED';
- :2082 release_task, 'the dependency auto-unblock (all `blockedOnTaskIds` DONE/ARCHIVED)'.
Each gains the strict-consumer rule: for a verified-local consumer each listed task needs retained verified delivery, and a missing id never counts. Use the full form with a pointer to **Strict dependent (CQ-V09)** under moe.claim_next_task Dependency gating (about :1465) in prose, and the short form in the code-comment lines. Check the wording against state/dependencyUnblock.ts dependencyShortfall and CLAUDE.md's sentence ('readiness means retained verified delivery, not merely DONE/ARCHIVED, and a missing prerequisite never satisfies it').

(d) comment-c16cb64b, point 1, at about :338 in get_context's **Execution policy context**. The sentence 'After a project rollback, an open attempt whose own snapshot is `verified-local` shows as `attemptSnapshot.profile: "verified-local"` under a non-strict `effectiveProfile`' holds only when the TASK snapshot is not verified-local, because a stored verified-local task snapshot floors effectiveProfile. Say that.

(e) comment-c16cb64b, point 2, at about :590 in moe.complete_task **Strict completion (CQ-F08)**. 'A task that was strict only through the live setting (its task and attempt snapshots are not `verified-local`) completes as legacy after the rollback' also covers a rollback to observe. Say 'after a rollback to `legacy` or `observe`', after confirming in tools/completeTask.ts and delivery/executionProfile.ts that an observe completion takes the legacy path.

(f) Line 1 reads '# Moe - MCP Seclaurveracl SpecifclaudeclaudeCication (Current)', an accidental edit in aa0c3766 ('multi account login', 2026-10-20). Restore it to '# Moe - MCP Server Specification (Current)', the text before that commit.

- One row per READINESS_IDS id (packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/executionReadiness.ts), all 15, in READINESS_IDS order, each id backticked.

Keep it terse: one line per row, as in the Local Runner table.
